blocks.content: Erosional and depositional landforms created by running water, wind, and glaciers reflect the distinct physical properties and kinetic energy of each geomorphic agent.

rows: High altitude and high latitude cold regions

items: V-shaped valleys are formed by rivers, whereas U-shaped valleys and hanging valleys are formed by glaciers.
Barchans (crescent-shaped dunes) and Loess are major wind depositional features frequently tested in competitive exams.
Cirques, Horns, and Aretes are classic glacial erosional landforms; Moraines, Drumlins, and Eskers are glacial depositional features.
Deltas, Ox-bow lakes, and Natural Levees develop in the lower/mature stages of river flow.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Running water is the most dominant geomorphic agent in humid regions, sculpting V-shaped valleys and expansive deltas.
Wind action decisionally predominates in arid regions, forming erosional features like yardangs and depositional landforms like barchans.
Glaciers shape high-altitude landscapes through plucking and abrasion, carving U-shaped valleys, cirques, and moraines.
Understanding the distinction between erosional and depositional landforms for each agent is essential for geography MCQs.
